entities.summary: German philosopher (1724-1804) whose Critique of Pure Reason and Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals transformed Western philosophy. His categorical imperative — act only according to maxims you could will as universal laws — became the foundation of modern deontological ethics and profoundly influenced legal and political theory.
